strings.name: Marc Rowan
strings.summary: Rowan moved from mergers and acquisitions into alternative investment, co-founding Apollo and later leading a model linking credit origination with insurance and retirement services. He became CEO in 2021 and chair in 2025. The model expands long-term financing while requiring management of liquidity, valuation and insurance liabilities.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded Apollo Global Management, advancing private credit, insurance asset management and alternative investing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Upbringing
strings.facts.f1.value: Grew up on Long Island, New York, before moving to Florida.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Wharton BS (1984) and finance MBA (1985), University of Pennsylvania.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Alternative investment platform
strings.highlights.h1.text: With partners, expanded from distressed investing into credit and real assets.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Asset management and insurance
strings.highlights.h2.text: Advanced Apollo’s integration with Athene, connecting investment capabilities with retirement savings.

strings.timeline.t4.title: Became CEO

strings.timeline.t6.text: Built the investment firm with former colleagues including Leon Black and Josh Harris.
strings.timeline.t7.title: MBA and finance career entry
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed Wharton’s MBA and joined Drexel’s mergers-and-acquisitions department.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed undergraduate studies
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned his Wharton bachelor’s degree, preparing for a finance career.
